chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): that he was asked about the khudr (turtle/tortoise) regarding
Is there zakat in it, and if it is sold for a large amount of wealth, he said, 'No, until a full year passes over it.'

key_terms.الْحَوْلُ: A full lunar year, the period required for zakat to become due on wealth or livestock
key_terms.الْخُضَرِ: Turtle or tortoise, specifically referring to the sea turtle or land tortoise in fiqh contexts

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zakat for turtles or tortoises (khudr) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the zakat ruling for *khudr* (a specific type of turtle or tortoise), establishing that it is exempt until a full lunar year (*hawl*) has passed, mirroring the criteria for other livestock. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of applying general zakat conditions to specific animals based on their classification as wealth (*mal*) rather than unique biological traits. The emphasis on the passage of time underscores the importance of *hawl* in determining the liability of zakat on movable assets in Shia fiqh.
